input.evidence_text: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed part of Bury Grammar School could now get a new lease of life Plans have been submitted to Bury council to convert part of the old school estate into new homes. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. Add-ons are also proposed for the latter two buildings which would see the existing single-storey extensions increased to two storeys

input.evidence_text: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed part of Bury Grammar School could now get a new lease of life Plans have been submitted to Bury council to convert part of the old school estate into new homes. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. Add-ons are also proposed for the latter two buildings which would see the existing single-storey extensions increased to two storeys

The late Labour veteran possessed an ingrained sense of public duty but perhaps it was this intens For years before smoking in pubs and restaurants was eventually outlawed in England in 2007, he was the passionate leader for a campaign to make Manchester smoke-free. Of course, he believed his adopted home city of Manchester should always be first His late mother had been seduced into addiction by images of the glamorous Hollywood greats, puffing away on the silver screen. So in 2004 he resolved to do something about a public health crisis which was blighting Manchester more than anywhere else in the country He had tried smoking at London School of Economics where he got a BSc in politics and economics and even tried a joint on a trip to Amsterdam but disliked it immediately. He admitted he 'couldn't deal with having a fire in my mouth' His campaigning went through many ups and downs but ended in victory, and probably helped to save lives. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. input.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
